item.title: We Talk About Mental Health. We Don't Fund It.
item.description:
Something has shifted in the way people talk about mental health.

The conversations have become more open. In certain circles, the old silence has started to break down. Young people especially have been more willing to speak honestly — about anxiety, about burnout, about the strain of navigating economies that demand a great deal and offer little security in return.

This change matters. Language shapes how problems get understood. Naming something is the first step toward addressing it.

item.title: Why We Stopped Being Bored — and What We Lost
item.description:
There used to be a moment on public transport that almost everyone knew.

You sat down. You had nothing in your hands. Your eyes drifted to the window, and your mind went somewhere — a half-formed thought, an old memory, a question that had been sitting at the back of your head for days. Nobody asked for that moment. It just happened.

Today, that moment barely gets a chance to show up.

item.title: The Digital Detox Guide: How to Reclaim Your Attention (Without Going Off-Grid)
item.description:
I watch my phone buzz and I check it without thinking. Three minutes later, I’ve somehow lost forty-five minutes to scrolling—not because I wanted to, but because the app kept feeding me content designed specifically to keep me scrolling. This pattern repeats a dozen times daily. I’m not unique. Most people reading this will recognize this exact experience.

Here’s what I’ve learned through investigation and genuine struggle: you’re not weak. You’re not lacking discipline. You’re fighting against technology that employs thousands of people specifically to make it addictive. That’s not a fair fight.
